title: Primes up to N
statement:
List every prime number up to and including `n`.

## Your function

```
int primes_up_to(int n, int *out);
```

Write the primes in ascending order into `out` and return how many there
were. The caller has made `out` big enough.

## Watch out

- `1` is not prime, and neither is anything below it. `2` is, and it is the
  only even prime.
- `n` may be `0` or negative: return `0` and write nothing.
- The sieve of Eratosthenes is the point. Mark a scratch array of `n + 1`
  flags: walk up from 2, and each time you meet an unmarked value, record it
  and mark all of its multiples. Testing every number against every smaller
  number also works, and is the thing the sieve exists to avoid.
- Marking can start at `value * value` -- anything smaller has already been
  marked by a smaller factor. Watch that product: it overflows an `int` long
  before `n` does.
- Whatever you allocate for the scratch flags, free it.

tests.name: zero
tests.description: No primes, and nothing printed after the count.

tests.name: two
tests.description: The first prime, and the only even one.
